pivotDirectionAudit.proof: For normalized positive share fractions p_j with sum 1, fixed-direction diagonal/rank losses are at least a_j/(D0 p_j). Cauchy gives sum a_j/p_j >= (sum sqrt(a_j))^2. Each rank component is a positive Gram form, so a negative interval lower endpoint is safely clamped to zero; the eighth diagonal losses are nonnegative. Row-radius subtraction is nonnegative and omitted, which only raises the upper bound. A strict comparison proves all allocations fail for this vector.

randomDirectionSearch.method: Seeded uniform perturbations of exact failing-pivot direction normalized to max coordinate 10^9; alpha grid {.01,.03,.1,.25,.5,1,2}; 100 directions each.

scope: Exact fixed-direction Cauchy tests for this finite original-coordinate comparison only; no claim over untested directions or the underlying Weil form.
